rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance – criminal history screening ban
rules.requirement: Berkeley rental housing providers may not ask about or use criminal history or criminal background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection, or decision-making. This includes refusing to rent, ending a tenancy, or charging a higher deposit or rent based on criminal history. A landlord who takes action based on criminal history must give the applicant or tenant written notice and a chance to respond.
citation_aliases: Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

enacted_date.quoted_span: On April 14, 2020, Berkeley City Council passed the Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance (BMC 13.106).

exemption_conditions.condition: Owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner of record lives in one of the units as their primary residence
Owner-occupied exemption applies only to properties with between 1 and 3 units
Limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties
Units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back to their home in accordance with BMC 13.76.130 A.9
exemption_conditions.value: owner move-back rental agreement per BMC 13.76.130 A.9

exemption_conditions.condition: Units occupied by existing tenant(s) seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates
exemption_conditions.value: existing tenant subletting or adding/replacing roommates

coverage.notes: The owner-occupied exemption needs both conditions: 1-3 units and owner residence. The public housing/Section 8 exemptions are limited; see the Ordinance for details.

rules.coverage_text: Rental housing providers in Berkeley, for current and prospective tenants.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner of record lives in one unit as their primary residence; units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back per BMC 13.76.130 A.9; units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.

tool_input.notes: This is the Berkeley Rent Board page summarizing the Berkeley ordinance. The page gives the City Council passage date but no effective date. Violations carry fines of $1,000 to $10,000 per violation; these are listed in the source but are not a separate rule.
